newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FORECAST-CSR yr net profit seen down again.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-CSR yr net profit seen down again.

text.p: Building materials, aluminium and sugar group CSR Ltd is expected to report its second consecutive annual profit fall on Monday, but profits are tipped for a rebound for 1997/98 as the local housing industry picks up.

Analysts contacted by Reuters forecast CSR to report a pre-abnormal net profit between A$208 million and A$226 million for the year to March 31, 1997. CSR's pre-abnormal net profit was A$320.1 million in 1995/96 and A$390.5 million in 1994/95.
However, analysts said the strengthening in the home construction market should push CSR's 1997/98 pre-abnormal net profits to between A$290 million and A$320 million.
Fabian Babich, building materials analyst at brokers ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, forecasts a pre-abnormal net profit of A$220 million for the 1996/97 year.
One Melbourne-based building materials analyst tipped a A$208 million pre-abnormal net profit for CSR, while a Sydney analyst estimated a pre-abnormal net profit of A$226 million.
Analyst forecast CSR to pay a 10 cent or 11 cent second half dividend, making the total 1996/97 dividend 22 or 23 cents.
In the 1996/97 first half, CSR reported a net profit before abnormals of A$154.7 million.
Analysts said the bright spots in CSR results should be its U.S. operations and aluminium, while the Australia businesses should be largely weaker.
"They would have to have a strong result next year and start getting some return on their heavy capital expenditure programme otherwise they will be in trouble," one analyst said.
He said CSR has invested over A$2 billion in the group's core operations over the past five years.
